ACENPs (acridine orange–ethidium bromide) induce apoptosis in cancer cells by increasing the expression of pro-apoptotic genes such as p53, Bax, Caspase3, and Caspase9 while downregulating anti-apoptotic genes. This was observed through DAPI staining showing nuclear fragmentation and condensation in a dose-dependent manner. Flow cytometry further confirmed that over 64% of MDA-MB-453 cells underwent apoptosis upon treatment with ACENPs.

In comparison, garlic EVs (extracellular vesicles) were found to be selectively taken up by kidney (A498) and lung (A549) cancer cells while showing no cytotoxicity in normal human dermal fibroblast (HDF) cells. Similarly, fingerroot-derived nanovesicles (FDNVs) were selectively taken up by colorectal cancer cells (HT-29 and HCT116), inducing apoptosis via the upregulation of Bax, caspase-3, and caspase-9 while downregulating Bcl-2 expression. Both garlic EVs and FDNVs demonstrated selective cytotoxicity towards cancer cells without affecting normal cells, highlighting their potential in targeted cancer therapy.
